_description: Phase 3 glossary backlog: Phase 1's 8 glossary-classified candidates plus 11 new terms discovered while mapping calculator query intent. Structured backlog only - no glossary pages exist yet.

fromPhase1Candidates.note: Platform-computed from auction eligibility data the user cannot supply; not honestly calculable from a plain formula.
Raw platform-reported unique-user count, not derived from other inputs.
A sum, not a derived rate; no meaningful calculate step beyond addition.
Raw count, not a derived calculation.
Simple average with thin standalone calculator demand.

newDiscoveries.note: Explains why the same spend/conversion data can produce different CAC/ROAS depending on the lookback window used - referenced from both, defined on neither.
Common point of confusion when a channel's ROAS looks low but it's actually assisting conversions credited elsewhere.
A conversion counted without a click - relevant context for CTR/ROAS pages without being a calculator itself.
Product-defined, not generic - the Activation Rate page references this term but shouldn't try to define it universally.
Underpins every retention/D1-D30 calculator; worth one shared definition instead of repeating it per page.
The methodology behind Incremental ROAS; a glossary page can carry the holdout-test explanation once.
Referenced by every experimentation calculator's power selector; one shared definition avoids repeating it four times.
Widely searched on its own ('what is a p-value'), separate from wanting to run a test.
Prerequisite concept for Incremental ROAS; not a calculator, but a common blocker query.
Underlies the (not-yet-built) A/B/n Bonferroni correction; worth defining once ahead of that build.
A recurring 'my test is significant but the lift is tiny' confusion; belongs next to the significance calculator, not inside it.
